title.value: t260 — categorical branching: fibration spine, push as Lan, lease generalization, global/local

summary.value: t260 goal: merge the t218 branching doctrine, the T249 worktree partition, and the t259 manifold axes/symmetries candidates into one categorical model of branching and push. SPINE (fibration): base B = A1 x A2 — identity poset (user < group < manifold-group) x placement poset (component < device < cloud); total category E = occupied workspaces (purpose x occupant x scope, t218); p: E -> B sends a workspace to its coordinate. CONJECTURE C1: p is a Grothendieck fibration — branch = cartesian lift f*W, a universal restriction to a new coordinate, data-only, emitting no HG rewrite (t218: a branch is a coordinate, not a tree node); worktree = the single filesystem realization of the lift, and T249 one-checkout-per-branch = split cleavage; merge = cocartesian pushforward, gated — existence of a lift never confers apply authority (mirrors M11/M12). PUSH = three phases, two directions: what moves is never a node-set but a log segment — an ordered diagram of rewrites plus closure under required relations and provenance — via (1) SELECT a purpose-keyed slice of one fold's content, (2) MATERIALIZE = F-lower onto a transport surface chosen by capability vector (t244; ordered log content rides reliable streams, presence rides datagrams, t231), (3) GATED INGEST = G, only if the receiving fold's M11/M12 gate admits, landing as NEW log entries in the receiver's sovereign log with the E2 trailer; a delivered slice that fails the gate has moved but changed nothing. CONJECTURE C4: push = Lan_f, pointwise colimit along a base morphism = t218 E4 merge; the E2 trailer is the comma-category data — no trailer, no colimit, no push. BRANCHING GENERALIZATION: any surface with restriction gets branches (MLIR regions per target, twin engine per device, per-principal branch-workspaces per t231 folder layout); branch-episode = lease (coordinate, occupant, purpose, placement) with at most one live occupant; git worktrees enforce the lease via filesystem, every other surface needs WF19 has-occupant; unoccupied branch = dormant S0 substrate (E3); no CRDT machinery needed — sovereign single-writer logs give per-log total order, merges are explicit reviewed events, merge-not-rebase preserves forward-only; GAP: no lease reclaim/expiry exists (same class as F1). GLOBAL VS LOCAL: no global writable memory; global = the URN namespace (URN-equality IS cross-fold identity, no cross-fold reference relation exists) + router :9000 read-only fan-in (the only legitimate cross-fold surface, R1); local = every realization — address, checkout, cache, twin fold — a memory add.

name.value: t260 spine — occupied workspaces fibered over identity x placement (conjecture C1)

content.value: CONJECTURE C1 — fibration spine of branching, derived in the sam.z440-cowork-workspace conversation (t260) from t218 + T249 + the t259 axis candidates. Base B = A1 x A2: the identity poset (user < group < manifold-group) times the placement poset (component < device < cloud). Total category E = occupied workspaces (purpose x occupant x scope, t218). Projection p: E -> B sends a workspace to its coordinate. Conjecture: p is a Grothendieck fibration. A branch is the cartesian lift f*W — the universal restriction of a workspace to a new coordinate; it carries data only, emits no HG rewrite, triggers no deploy (t218: a branch is a coordinate, not a tree node; branch name = flattened WF19 tuple <lane>/<purpose-slug>). A worktree is the single filesystem realization of the lift; T249 one-checkout-per-branch = split cleavage — exactly one chosen lift per (branch, base morphism). A merge is the cocartesian pushforward and is gated: existence of a lift never confers apply authority (mirrors M11/M12; promotion to trunk is always an explicit reviewed act).

name.value: t260 push — log-segment transport in three phases; push = Lan_f (conjecture C4)

content.value: CONJECTURE C4 — push as gated log-segment transport, derived in the sam.z440-cowork-workspace conversation (t260). What moves is never a node-set; it is a log segment — an ordered diagram of rewrites plus closure under required relations and provenance. Three phases, two directions: (1) SELECT a purpose-keyed slice of one fold's content; (2) MATERIALIZE = F-lower onto a transport surface chosen by capability vector (workstation kind x engine endpoint x rewrite-reach x surface-reach, t244) — ordered log content rides reliable streams, presence rides datagrams (t231); (3) GATED INGEST = G, only if the receiving fold's M11/M12 gate admits, landing as NEW log entries in the receiver's sovereign log with the E2 trailer (authored-by agent/session/purpose; E5 adds user/workstation/channel-kind when disambiguating). A delivered slice that fails the gate has moved but changed nothing. Formal reading: push = Lan_f, the pointwise colimit along a base morphism = the t218 E4 merge; the E2 trailer is the comma-category data — no trailer, no colimit, no push (a checkable well-definedness criterion). Idempotence is by URN identity (SeedIfAbsent grow-set), not by protocol. Engine code is itself an F-projection of operad + fold semantics (t244); pushing it = re-lowering / bootstrapped provisioning through the build gate — the ANALOG of the apply gate, not the same gate — and emits no HG rewrite.

name.value: t260 branching generalization — branch-episode as lease (conjecture)

content.value: CONJECTURE — branching generalization, derived in the sam.z440-cowork-workspace conversation (t260). Any surface with restriction gets branches: MLIR module per target (branches as regions, not modules), twin engine per device, per-principal branch-workspaces (t231 folder layout). A branch-episode is a lease: (coordinate, occupant, purpose, placement) with at most one live occupant. Git worktrees enforce the lease via the filesystem (T249 one-checkout-per-branch); every other surface needs WF19 has-occupant to enforce the same invariant. An unoccupied branch is dormant S0 substrate (t218 E3 — occupancy is liveness). No CRDT machinery is needed: sovereign single-writer logs give per-log total order; merges are explicit reviewed events, never eventual convergence; merge-not-rebase preserves forward-only. GAP: no lease reclaim/expiry mechanism exists — same class as F1.
